question: The distance of the point P(2, 3) from the x-axis is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **distance** of any point **P(x, y)** from the **x-axis** is always equal to the absolute value of its **y-coordinate** (ordinate).

Given point: **P(2, 3)**

Here, x = 2 and **y = 3**.

∴ Distance from x-axis = |y| = 3 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Coordinates of point **P = (2, 3)**.

**Formula Used:** Perpendicular distance of **P(x₁, y₁)** from the line **ax + by + c = 0** is |ax₁ + by₁ + c| / √(a² + b²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b80b9d297d81d82cada752285cd895b5af5ae4f15bd4572f3b54e923f58ac41e.png] 

The equation of the **x-axis** is **y = 0**.

⇒ Here, a = 0, b = 1, and c = 0.

⇒ Distance = |(0 × 2) + (1 × 3) + 0| / √(0² + 1²)

⇒ Distance = |3| / 1

⇒ Distance = 3 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distance from y-axis

The distance of a point **P(x, y)** from the **y-axis** is the absolute value of its x-coordinate, i.e., **|x|**.

Distance from Origin

The distance of a point **P(x, y)** from the **origin (0, 0)** is calculated using the formula **√(x² + y²)**.

Coordinates on Axes

Any point on the **x-axis** has a y-coordinate of 0, **(x, 0)**. Any point on the **y-axis** has an x-coordinate of 0, **(0, y)**.</p
